elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..." — the three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay sentence is fully replaced, and no other provision reimposes a minimum (7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges; 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume commitment).

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.1: "...and will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term," consistent with 7.1 (Fees stated in each Order Form, usage-based unit pricing permitted).

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: after the edit no purchase commitment of any duration exists, so there is no multi-year exposure to confine to a 12-month term.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: with no commitment remaining in 2.1 there is nothing to reduce; the removed "without reduction or termination rights" language is gone.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no minimum means no shortfall can arise, and no take-or-pay or penalty formula is retained anywhere (7.1 also bars undisclosed minimum-use charges).

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single in-place replacement of 2.1 delivers both elements in operative language (no minimum purchase or volume commitment; payment only for Services used or ordered).

Minimality holds: exactly one sentence was replaced, with no survival tails, procedures, at-own-expense language, or extra requirements added, and favourable existing text in 7.1 and 12.3 was left untouched.

Intent preserved: 7.1's Order Form fee mechanic and fixed-fee/usage-price structure and 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement now align with 2.1 rather than contradict it; no cross-reference to the deleted take-or-pay sentence exists, so no dangling references or undefined terms result.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no commitment survives; the comment correctly holds the 12-month/30-day/true-up structure in reserve without importing it into the operative text.
No repair needed; the deviation classification is correct because the original three-year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights is walk-away territory.
